title: Channel Letters with Jimmy DiResta: Template, Edge Wrapping, and LED Sign Assembly
summary: Jimmy DiResta demonstrates a hands-on build of a backlit channel-letter sign. The project starts from a laser-cut logo template, then glue-tits are attached to plywood and cut into letters with a bandsaw (or a jig saw as an alternative). A circle-template guides even LED light distribution across all letters, followed by edge-wrapping each letter with aluminum flashing, and assembling the pieces with hot glue, nails, and spacers to hide wiring. The interior faces are primed, painted (on both sides), and the LED strips are installed from the back, sealed with silicone for durability, before a final power-test reveal. The video emphasizes practical, accessible techniques for custom channel-letter signage using common shop tools and inexpensive materials.

sections.title: Intro: what makes a channel letter a channel letter
sections.description: Explains the defining feature of channel letters: a side wall that traps and bounces light inside the letter to create a glowing silhouette.

sections.title: Logo template via laser cut
sections.description: Jimmy uses a laser-cut version of the logo as a stencil/template to guide the lettering. He notes printer absence and uses laser-cut letters as the source for the plywood template.

sections.title: Gluing letters to plywood for stencil
sections.description: The letters are glued to plywood with spray adhesive to create a stable stencil that will be kept for later use.

sections.title: Cutting letters on bandsaw (with jigsaw as alternative)
sections.description: With a template in place, the letters are cut out on the bandsaw for speed and precision; Jim notes that a bandsaw is preferred, but a jigsaw can work as an alternative.

sections.title: LED lighting plan and distribution
sections.description: They plan the light layout, using 48 LED lights (24 per package) and a circle template to distribute lights evenly across the letters.

sections.title: Hole preparation for LED strips
sections.description: Holes are drilled to receive the LED strings; the plan is to evenly disperse light and maintain clean wiring channels.

sections.title: Sanding and surface prep
sections.description: Letters are sanded to a smooth finish to prepare for painting and prevent splinters or hand injuries during handling.

sections.title: Edge-wrapping with roof flashing
sections.description: Edges are wrapped with four-inch aluminum flashing. The wrap is done in segments and joined at flat areas to avoid overstressing curved sections.

sections.title: Temporary bonding and final fastening
sections.description: Hot glue provides temporary tack for alignment, followed by finishing with nails to secure the assembly. The joins are placed where the edges flatten to reduce stress.

sections.title: Priming and two-sided painting plan
sections.description: Interior faces are primed white to reflect light. The letters are planned to be flipped and painted from the back to prevent bleed-through on the visible faces.

sections.title: Back-side LED installation
sections.description: LED strips are installed from the back; wires are tucked behind letters with hot glue for initial placement and silicone for long-term sealing.

sections.title: Panel joining and spacing strategy
sections.description: Two-inch-by-halftime spacing blocks are used to keep letters aligned and to line up mounting hardware with spacer blocks previously installed.

sections.title: Power test and reveal
sections.description: The assembled sign is powered, tested, and revealed as a functioning backlit letter display with wiring concealed behind the letters.

sections.title: Materials recap
sections.description: Wrap-up notes emphasize that the project uses simple materials (plywood, flashing, basic LED strips) that are widely available.

featured_techniques.technique: Edge wrapping with roof flashing to create a sanitary light seal
Distributing LED light evenly using a circle template
Back-side wiring and silicone sealing for long-term durability
Two-sided painting approach to prevent bleed-through
